# Review: cid-tiradas-115-117 (tiradas 115–117, vv. 2338–2402)

Checked against the pinned packet; Pidal 1923, PDF pp. 279–284 (printed 275–280: text and italics, the rubrics of
tiradas 115, 116, 117 (and 118), the 22 lines of italic chronicle prose on pp. 275–276, and the footnotes 2338,
2342, 2347, 2348, 2351, 2356, 2357, 2360, 2362, 2363, 2364, 2365, 2366, 2367 [= 2376], 2370, 2371, 2375, 2379,
2381, 2383, 2388, 2391, 2398, 2400, 2401, and the * note on la delantera); the established text of v. 319
(tirada 18) for the cross-reference; the published parts (01-04 for paragogic -e in `l`, 18-18, 19-23, 44-48,
83-83b, 112-114) for house renderings; `conventions.md`; `known-forms.json`, `novel-forms.json`; the last line
of LOG.md.
`t` integrity (by script, before and after the edits): all `t` joined by "\n" equal the 66 packet verses
(2361b included) in order; 28 units, none across a tirada break; every `l` has as many lines as its `t`; no `t`
was touched. Both files edited by script (json load/replace/dump, indent 1, ensure_ascii=False).

## Pass 1: units.json

1. 2338 · n · **style** · "about fifty lines by Pidal's reckoning": the rubric says "50 versos" flat (as fixed
   in 112-114). Done: "fifty lines". The rest of the lost-folio note checked against the italic prose on
   pp. 275–276: Búcar's message (leave Valencia in peace, sinón … le pecharie quanto y avie fecho), the Çid's
   answer (ante destos tres días), the Infantes asking for la delantera (with Pidal's * note quoted exactly),
   Fernando, Aladraf, his flight (fuxó, que solamente non lo osó esperar), Pero Vermúdez killing the Moor and
   giving Fernando the horse (yo otorgarlo e con vusco), the prose ending on Fernando's "mucho vos gradesco lo
   que dezides;": all right; prose not included, the chronicle named, per conventions. The Frère anecdote
   (note 2338) is a fair summary of Pidal's note.
2. 2339 (vv. 2339–40) · i · **weak** · "The two rode back together to the company": en una conpaña is
   'together, in one company' (the glosser's broaden of una says so), not a return "to the company"; and
   "bears out every word" overstates otorga … quomo se alaba. Done: "The two came back together, and Don Pero
   bears out Fernando's boasting."
3. 2348 (vv. 2348–49) · n · **style** · "Pidal's note: entre, v. 191: entre X e Y, 'X and Y together, both'"
   reads as if the gloss were Pidal's; his note is only "entre, v. 191". Done: "Pidal's note on entre refers to
   v. 191; entre X e Y, 'X and Y together, both'."
4. 2352 (vv. 2352–54) · n · **weak** · "the familiar singular (tú), where elsewhere the poem's speakers use
   vos": untrue as a general claim (the angel in the Çid's dream slips into tú, the townsfolk use tú to the Çid, both
   noted in published parts). Done: "the familiar singular (tú), not the courteous vos." The label (cúriesme,
   present subjunctive 2nd sg. + ethic me) is right.
5. 2361b, 2362–63, 2364–65, 2367, 2371–72 · l · **style** · the paragogic e's were shown by bracketing a letter
   of the English ("loya[l]", "will-mak[e]", "shar[e]", "it-shall-see[m]", "will-b[e]", "leisur[e]",
   "to-see[k]", "to-kil[l]"), which tells the reader a letter of the English word is restored. House practice
   (01-04: razón[e] "saying", señor[e] "lord", son[e] "are", dolor[e] "grief") leaves the English plain; the note
   explains the e. Done: plain words. Whole-word restorations ([estave] "[is]") and restored letters inside a
   word with an English counterpart (a[s], h[i]s, w[as], fi[e]ld, [b]roken, [h]as) kept, as in the house.
6. 2362 (vv. 2362–63) · i + l · **weak** · `i` "The Creator will win this battle … you have your share with him":
   the note quotes Pidal rightly — con él avedes part 'tenéis con él favor, acogida' — and the `i` then ignores
   him; "will win" also says more than fera(ve) 'will make, bring about'. Done: `i` "This battle will be the
   Creator's doing, and you are so worthy that you stand in his favour."; `l` "you-have part".
7. 2366 · i · **style** · "We shall see it through": 'see it through' is 'persevere', not Verlo hemos 'we shall
   see it'. Done: "We shall see it done, with God and with your good fortune."
8. 2368 (vv. 2368–69) · i + n · **error** · `i` "before the Campeador, a man always attended by good fortune"
   gave the auze to the Çid while the note said "read with the bishop, the subject of the line". Done: `i` "ever
   attended by good fortune, he planted himself before the Campeador:"; the note now says the phrase is read
   with the bishop here, though it could go with the Campeador, whose auze Minaya has just invoked (v. 2366).
   Pidal's note to 2366 (auze, 'ventura', 2369, 1523) is cited rightly.
9. 2370 (vv. 2370–72) · n · **error** · "Pidal's note: La misa de santa Trinidad, v. 319 — the mass said before
   battle": v. 319 (established text, tirada 18) is the mass the abbot of San Pedro de Cardeña is to say at dawn
   before the Çid rides into exile, a votive mass (18-18), not a battle mass. Done: the gloss now says what
   v. 319 is.
10. 2370 · i · **style** · "Today I sang you the mass": dix = 'I said'; "sang" is a stock lift. Done: "Today I
    said the mass of the Holy Trinity for you."
11. 2381 (vv. 2380–82) · i · **weak** · "go and try your hand on them" while the note quotes Pidal ensayar,
    'acometer', 3318 ('to attack'). Done: "go and attack them." `l` "to-try" kept (the note sets out the three
    senses of ensayar in vv. 2376, 2381, 2388).

Checked and kept:
- Every quotation attributed to Pidal verified on the scan: 2338 (incl. the Frère/Romana/Robertson story), 2342
  (comp. v. 300), 2347 (p. 107), 2348 (v. 191), 2351 (¡ola!, vv. 2169, 2177, Muño Gustioz), 2356 (ayo), 2357
  (v. 230), 2360, 2362 (ferave, comp. v. 15, Trinidade, Pedro Abad), 2363, 2364, 2365, 2366, 2367 (tengamos
  calma), 2370 (v. 319), 2371, 2375 (Verso dudoso … hereditarios en las familias, exact), the note printed
  "2367" (ensayar 'probar, usar un arma', 2414, 3663 …) rightly reassigned to 2376, 2379, 2381 (3318), 2383
  (espolonada, exact), 2388 (2460; 2746, 2781), 2391 (v. 713), 2398 ('victoria'), 2400 (v. 1141-42), 2401
  ('tenían muchas labores o adornos'; tendal obrado, 1783). All exact; none invented.
- Rubrics 115, 116, 117 quoted exactly; English versions fair.
- Grammar labels confirmed: vea, meresca, cúriesme, cúrielos, tengades, ayamos (present subjunctive); quisiere,
  fuere, semejar[e] (future subjunctive); plogiesse, pudiesse (imperfect subjunctive); serien, querría,
  veriedes (conditional); abrán, podredes, fincarán, fera[ve], sera[ve], verlo hemos (futures, split future);
  vieran (-ra pluperfect indicative); Plogo, nasco, dix, vin, priso (strong preterites); Parávas, Ensayavas,
  ívalos, dávanle (imperfect + enclitic); Mandádno'los, idlos, plazme, nol, quel, m' incal, d' aquent.
- House renderings: Minaya Álvar Fáñez, Per Vermudoz, Diego / Fernando for Dí[a]go / Dí[da]go / Ferrando,
  Don Jerome, Babieca, Búcar, the en buen ora formula, amor "favour" (2379). Consistent.
- Italic brackets described rightly; the two least-sure italics (ca[n]po 2343, [a] 2359) are flagged as LOG.md
  has them.

Refused / left as drafted:
- 2383 `i` "led the charge" for priso a espolonada (Pidal 'comenzó el ataque'; a charge of a few knights ahead
  of the host): the bishop does exactly that. Left.
- 2382 n "the line has a smile in it": commentary, but true to the scene and mild. Left.
- 2400–01 `i` "so richly worked were they": follows Pidal's 'tenían muchas labores o adornos'; tantas (fem.)
  against tendales (masc.) is left unexplained in Pidal too. Left.
- 2398 `i` "It pleased God that this should be the victory": a fair reading of Plogo a Dios, aquesta fo el
  arrancada. Left.
- `l` keeps restored letters inside English words (a[s] for qu[o]mo, h[i]s for s[o]s): house practice. Left.

Pass 1 counts: error 2 · weak 4 · style 5 (11 items).

## Pass 2: gloss.json

1. estave · **error** · "estar — he was (imperfect 3rd sg. estava with Pidal's restored paragogic -e,
   estav[e]…; = estaba)": wrong tense and wrong bracket. The whole word [estave] is Pidal's, and it is está +
   paragogic e with a bridging v, like fera[ve] / sera[ve], as the unit says. Done: 'he is', present, = está.
2. cúriesme · **error** · "present subjunctive 2nd sg. used as a polite imperative": the 2nd singular is the
   familiar tú (the unit says so). Done: "used as a command, the familiar tú".
3. ferave · **weak** · "base … 'fera' = fará, with an added ending -ve": ferá (= hará), and the unit's analysis
   is paragogic -e + bridging v, with Pidal's 'ferave "hará", con -e paragógica'. Done; notes and glossary agree.
4. serave · **weak** · same; also misprinted "seráve" and "will be (discharged)". Done, with Pidal's 'habrá de
   cumplirse la obligación que cada uno tiene'.
5. semejare · **weak** · "future subjunctive … or infinitive with paragogic -e; reading not certain": Pidal's
   'de la parte que os pareciere' settles it as future subjunctive, as the unit has. Done.
6. meresca · **weak** · "the exact sense of 'deserve of you' is not certain": Pidal glosses it fully
   ('ojalá os lo pueda pagar con creces'; 'merezca de vos el doble'). Done.
7. señal · **weak** · "blazoned … the heraldic sense is likely but not certain": Pidal says 'armas con un emblema
   pintado' and warns that such signs were not yet hereditary blazons. Done.
8. ensayar · **weak** · one sense with "i.e. attack" tacked on; Pidal distinguishes 'probar, usar un arma'
   (2376) and 'acometer' (2381). Done.
9. espolonada · **weak** · "he set off spurring, at a gallop": Pidal 'comenzó el ataque', the charge of a few
   knights ahead of their host. Done.
10. ensayavas · **weak** · "went into action, tried his hand … put himself to the test": Pidal 'esforzarse en la
    lucha, hacer proezas'. Done.
11. falssan · **weak** · "sense from context": Pidal's note (falssar las armas defensivas, v. 713). Done.
12. huebras · **weak** · "with such labour(?)'; the sense of this phrase is uncertain": Pidal 'tenían muchas
    labores o adornos'; comp. tendal obrado, 1783. Done: 'work, ornament'.
13. orden · **weak** · "fem. here": nothing in mi orden or the las that picks up orden e manos shows the gender.
    Done: "(noun)".
14. __broaden__ amo · **weak** · "closest ayo, tutor; from context": the sense is Pidal's ('ayo' que cuida a un
    joven que hace sus primeras armas). Done.
15. __broaden__ a · **weak** · "a espolonada — 'at a gallop, spurring'": as 9. Done: prender a espolonada 'to
    begin the attack, charge' (Pidal).
16. __broaden__ priso · **weak** · "'he spurred off, charged'": as 9. Done.
17. __broaden__ part · **weak** · missing: con él avedes part 'you have favour with him' (Pidal 'tenéis con él
    favor, acogida'); the known entry has only share, side, aside. Added.
18. __broaden__ idlos · **weak** · missing: the known entry ties idlos to "the next verb conortar"; here idlos
    ensayar 'go and attack them' (Pidal 'acometer'). Added.
19. otorga · **style** · "grants, consents, agrees": here 'confirms, bears out' Fernando's claim. Done.
20. ala · **style** · Pidal's '¡ola!' added; "Come now, Pero Vermúdez!" → the text's Per Vermudoz.
21. querríalas · **style** · "split form querer + ía": no split here; querría + enclitic las. Done.
22. ívalos · **style** · "ir a + inf. without a" → "ir + bare infinitive"; íva → iva.
23. trinidade · **style** · "old form with final -e": it is the manuscript's own paragogic -e, Pidal's model
    (note 2362). Done.
24. corças · **style** · hedge replaced by Pidal's own words (Verso dudoso. Parece que … por señal o blasón).

Checked and kept: otorga's lemma line, alaba, ueste, nunca, vieran, nuevos, maravillan, díago, dídago, serien,
caro, cúrielos, quier, fuere, leale, dinno, mandádno, qual, conplir, verlo, vagare, parávas, dix, salí, vin,
matare, plogiesse, pudiesse, aquent, crebado, çercavan, dávanle, enbraçó, escudo, abaxó, asta, abatió, cade,
cuerdas; __broaden__ tanto, una, delant, amor, con, cabo, alcança, buscare (future subjunctive kept as the known
reading, the infinitive + paragogic -e added: it agrees with the unit's note on buscar[e]/matar[e]), fincava,
sabor, avía, armas, pagar, quitar, cómmo, matava, entrava, sacan, vuestros.
Keys of gloss.json minus __broaden__ equal novel-forms.json (57). Every __broaden__ (24, 2 added) is the
known-forms entry whole + " · also " + the new reading (checked by script). The other known forms were checked
against this part's uses; aun, ya, entre, mas ('most'), hemos, huviar, cueta, incal, debdo, ha, fincarán,
canpo, tornados, arrancada ('victoria'), acostarse, tendales, albergada, afevos, afé, ojo, abbat, coraçón
already cover them.

Refused:
- dinno "nn sounded ñ": plausible for the spelling and harmless. Left.
- nuevos "new to this, unseasoned": a fair shade of nuevos son llegados beside 'newly arrived'. Left.
- quier "subjunctive in value; = quiera": qui quier = quienquiera; harmless beside the unit's "cut-down quiere".
  Left.

## For conventions.md
- Paragogic -e in `l`: the English word stays plain (leal[e] "loyal", vagar[e] "leisure"), as in 01-04; brackets
  in `l` only for restored words or letters with an English counterpart.
- auze "good fortune" in `i`; ensayar in its three senses (2376 'try', 2381 'attack', 2388 refl. 'exert
  oneself'), from Pidal.
